goldens.comment: The test test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling has a docstring that doesn't match the test implementation.
goldens.reasoning: None of the candidates point out that the docstring of test_thread_queue_parallel_error_handling doesn't match what the test does. C1 is about complete_offset being called on errors, which is a different issue.

candidates: complete_offset is called unconditionally in the finally block, even when result_processor raises, making failed work items appear successfully processed and allowing the commit loop to advance offsets, potentially skipping/losing messages. Only mark the offset completed after the work item was processed successfully and avoid completing on shutdown paths.

get_committable_offsets can incorrectly commit past missing offsets after a prior commit. After mark_committed prunes offsets ≤ committed, min_offset may jump forward over a gap, and start = max(last_committed + 1, min_offset) will skip the missing offset and allow committing later ones. Add an explicit gap check so we never advance commits past last_committed + 1 unless that offset has been observed and completed.

The thread-queue-parallel strategy starts a background commit thread; the test only calls factory.shutdown() which stops the queue workers but never closes the returned consumer, so the commit thread can keep running and mutate state after assertions and leak into other tests. Close the strategy before shutting down the factory and apply similarly in the other new thread-queue-parallel tests.
